articles.title: Joel Klatt's CFP Reaction: Does Indiana Still Have CFP Path? Klatt's Playoff Tiers
articles.summary: Alabama, UCLA both fall and Indiana's College Football Playoff path might be over after the fourth CFP rankings of the season.
articles.body: The fourth College Football Playoff rankings of the season shuffled things around, but what happened to the defending national champions, and which teams still have a playoff path? The Indiana Hoosiers fell six spots to No. 14 following their overtime loss to Washington. At No. 14, the Hoosiers would be the third team out of the CFP bracket and miss the playoffs. For FOX Sports' Joel Klatt, the Hoosiers should still earn a postseason bid. Additionally, Alabama dropped three spots to No. 6 behind Texas and Tennessee, and UCLA's first loss dropped them five spots to No. 9. Here are Klatt's CFP takeaways and CFP tiers following Tuesday night's rankings: Should Indiana Have Fallen 6 Spots After Washington Loss? Klatt's thoughts: "They are getting crushed. They're 9-2. Their best wins are now both ranked Nebraska and USC. Their strength of schedule is 40th. Not great, but you certainly know as good or better than some others up there in the top 10. And then their win-loss versus the top 25. They're 2-2. Now here's what's fascinating about this, and I want to preface this by saying I really like Alabama. I like Keelon Russell a lot. I think it's a really good defense. I don't want to play Alabama, but their résumé is actually a résumé that is worse than Indiana's. Now there is a Grand Canyon in between these two teams, and those two teams played last year. "I’m not saying they should be ranked based on last year. Fernando Mendoza is not walking through those doors, so I fully understand that. Alabama is a better version of what they were a year ago. There's no question about that, defensively and running the football. But if you look at Alabama's résumé, they're also 9-2. They're 0-2 against the top 25, and their strength of schedule is 18th. … Win-loss vs. top 25, Alabama is 0-2. Their best wins are now Kentucky and LSU, both unranked. Now, their strength of schedule is still solid. There's no doubt, but that's there. Yet again, there's a Grand Canyon in between these two teams in terms of where they're at in the rankings. I would just say, if Indiana was a different brand that had a national championship last year, had won 25 of their last 27, and just, just with that résumé, just like take the logos. But if you just put this blind, and you were to say like, ‘Well, what do you think?’ You would say, ‘Oh, they're probably right near each other, right?’ No, no, they're not even close. One's getting the wild benefit of the doubt, and the other is not. And yet, Indiana is the team that's the reigning national champ. "I just find it incredibly bold of this College Football Playoff committee to basically say, ‘Hey, Indiana, you're out unless wild chaos ensues,’ Now they could probably make the argument like, ‘No, there's a path they could get to Indianapolis and play for the Big Ten championship game,’ Yeah, but it's narrow. Look at some of these scenarios. So, Indiana would have to win. That's obvious. And Iowa, Minnesota and Oregon win, and UCLA loses." Does Indiana Have A Shot At The CFP? Klatt's thoughts: "So you're telling me that the defending champ needs absolute chaos just to sniff the college football playoff in a 12-team era, and we're just going to throw BYU in there. I get it. BYU beat Notre Dame, but like out of the Big 12, really? We're just going to throw Wake Forest in there. I get it. They're only a one-loss team, and I like Wake Forest a lot, a lot. But we all know that the most difficult football is played in the SEC, in the Big Ten, and you're just going to shove Indiana out of the playoff? That is bold, committee. That is bold. "I mean, any other brand and everyone would be up in arms. Everyone would be up in arms. And again, I'm just going to say this: I really like Alabama. Alabama is a heck of a football team. When I watch their film, I think that they could easily win the national championship. I'm not suggesting that Alabama should be 14th. I'm just saying, have a little respect for what Curt Cignetti and Indiana have done, not only this year, but in his tenure there. They're certainly not getting that right now. "So Indiana is 6-2 against teams with winning records. Only Texas has more wins against teams with winning records. They've got eight games versus teams with winning records. Only behind Texas and Oregon among playoff contenders. Alabama is 4-2 against teams with winning records. Indiana is 6-2 against teams with winning records. Like, they're getting crushed. That's why I can only speculate that this is personal. The committee has made it personal. [They] clearly have made it personal with Curt Cignetti. There's no other reason that Indiana is No. 14 and that far away from a résumé like Alabama's or Wake Forest or BYU, and just on the outside looking in, you're just going to shove them out of the playoff. They're not even going to get a chance to compete for a national championship. "If they beat Purdue and go 10-2, does anyone really believe deep down in their heart that a 10-2 team from either the SEC or the Big Ten should not go to the College Football Playoff? Listen, I’m not suggesting that the Big Ten is the SEC this year. The SEC is the better conference this year. They've got better top-end teams. That's where the strength of the conference or conference debate lies. Their quarterback play has been better. The SEC is better this year. I'm not saying Indiana should be ranked higher than Alabama or Tennessee or Texas. No, that's not what I'm suggesting at all. I'm suggesting that they should be given a little bit of respect for what they're doing. Their résumé is not that bad." Klatt's Newest CFP Tiers CFP Power Four Locks: Georgia, Utah, Notre Dame, Miami Klatt's thoughts: "My locks are Georgia, Utah, Notre Dame, and Miami. I think those four are in. Georgia's in the SEC championship game. Utah is in the Big 12 championship game. Yeah, yeah. Miami is in the ACC championship game, and obviously, even if Notre Dame loses, they're just not going to lose. What are they? 27-point favorites, 24, something along those lines. I mean, it's something crazy." Comfortable: Texas, Alabama, Tennessee Klatt's thoughts: "Comfortable is Texas. They seem firmly in. Even if they were to lose to Texas A&M, they've got so many good wins. That's the best two loss résumé in America, no questions asked. And that's a team that I don't want to face. In particular, if they ever got to a point where they were running the football more efficiently, because Arch Manning is playing better. He played great last week. Their defense is excellent. Alabama's defense is excellent. They can throw the ball with Keelon Russell. Then you've got the run defense combination for Tennessee. "I think these teams are comfortably in, as they should be. I want to see these teams in the playoff. There's no doubt, and we're probably going to get one of those teams get a bye. I think if Texas goes to the SEC championship game, they'll probably stay in the top four and get a bye, and then we'll see the other two host a first-round playoff game. I think that would be pretty good." On The Bubble: BYU, Texas Tech, Wake Forest, UCLA, Indiana, Oregon Klatt's thoughts: "On the bubble, because these are teams that I just think have to win. BYU has to win. If they lose, they would probably be out. Texas Tech has to win, or they would probably be out. Wake Forest. Here's the only reason I put Wake Forest here is if for some crazy reason — and I know I have Miami as a lock, and I know I'm not being intellectually consistent here — but if for some crazy reason, Wake Forest were to lose this weekend and in the ACC championship game, then… I don't know. "UCLA is clearly on the bubble; they have to win. I had made this graphic before seeing this. Indiana is not on the bubble. They are the kids that couldn't afford the tickets, and they're like peering over the fence right now. So that's where Indiana is, and then Oregon. Oregon is right there. They moved up after their win, UCLA lost, Indiana lost." So You're Telling Me There's A Chance: Iowa, USC Klatt's thoughts: "Iowa, there's a chance there. They could be a 10 and two play for the Big 10 championship game. That's not out of the question. "And then guys, I know, I know you're all gonna throw up here. But USC, with a wild weekend — for instance, okay, they beat UCLA. BYU loses. TCU beats Tech. Washington beats Oregon. Nebraska beats Iowa, and Purdue beats Indiana. That's not insane, right? I mean, it's crazy, and it's wild, but it's not insane. And USC would kind of be right there, so you're telling me there's a chance." Maybe Next Year: Ohio State Klatt's thoughts: "And then there's a ‘maybe next year’ category, and that one was a team that was in last week and had a chance on the bubble. Now Ohio State, better luck next year. Very disappointing for the preseason No. 1. They're kind of my first team that we've been talking about as playoff contenders that lost last weekend, and then they're kind of out." articles.title: "His DMs kinda went ding ding": Why Kevin Hayes says NHL goaltender Joel Hofer's reported connection with Charli D'Amelio should not be called dating
articles.summary: Kevin Hayes spills the tea on NHL goaltender Joel Hofer's surprising encounter with TikTok star Charli D'Amelio, clarifying their relationship status amidst dating rumors.
articles.body: Kevin Hayes has kicked up the rumor mill regarding Joel Hofer and Charli D’Amelio’s relationship, spilling the tea on their supposed meeting. In an interview on the Spittin’ Chiclets podcast, Hayes said the St. Louis Blues goaltender and the social media personality reportedly met in the elevator before their interactions grew.Hayes's comments put a new spin on the dating rumors that began in 2024. But his choice of words was especially notable, as he referred to the connection without confirming the two were officially dating.Kevin Hayes reveals Joel Hofer's Charli D'Amelio encounterKevin Hayes described Joel Hofer and Charli D'Amelio's reported first meeting as an unexpected elevator encounter. According to the NHL forward, the interaction eventually led to messages between the St. Louis Blues goaltender and the TikTok personality."I wouldn't call it dating… [Hofer and Charli D'Amelio] ran into each other on an elevator. His DMs kinda went ding ding, and we were there for a couple nights, and the rest is history," Hayes said during the podcast appearance.His comments suggest that the connection developed after the two crossed paths, although Hayes deliberately avoided describing it as a confirmed romantic relationship.The revelation is particularly interesting because Hayes played alongside Hofer during the 2023-24 season with the St. Louis Blues. That experience placed him in the same team environment during the period when the rumors first began circulating.Rumors began to circulate about Joel Hofer and Charli D’Amelio in late March 2024. Discussions on social media, including posts from the TikTok-focused account TeaTokTalk, hinted that the pair may have been getting to know each other.Joel Hofer is a Canadian professional ice hockey goaltender for the St. Louis Blues of the NHL. The Winnipeg native was selected by the franchise with the 107th overall pick in the 2018 NHL Draft.Hofer also represented Canada at the 2020 World Junior Championship, helping the national team capture gold. In June 2025, he signed a two-year, $6.8 million contract extension with St. Louis, carrying an average annual value of $3.4 million through the 2026-27 season.Charli D'Amelio's popularity and previous hockey connectionsOne of the biggest TikTok personalities, Charli D’Amelio rose to fame with her dance videos and social media posts. She was the first creator to hit 100 million followers on TikTok, and has since branched out into entertainment and business ventures.Comparisons were drawn between her rumored link-up with Hofer and her sister Dixie D'Amelio’s previously reported romance with NHL forward Trevor Zegras.The two stories show how connections between pro hockey players and big social media personalities can draw attention beyond the NHL audience.But the distinction still matters to Hofer and Charli. articles.title: NHL Power Rankings for Every Team at Thanksgiving 2026
articles.summary: It's a significant milepost in the NHL season.
articles.body:
It's a significant milepost in the NHL season.

Roughly three-quarters of teams that have found themselves in playoff spots upon the arrival of American Thanksgiving this century have made the tournament field come springtime. In fact, exactly 12 of 16 teams accomplished the task in 2025-26.

But that's neither a death knell nor a guarantee as the holiday meal approaches.

The Edmonton Oilers came from two points below the cutline to make the Western Conference field last season, while the Buffalo Sabres came from five points off the pace to get their names on the eight-team Eastern Conference bracket.

On the flip side, the New Jersey Devils were first in the Metropolitan Division and wound up missing the postseason entirely after sinking all the way to seventh.

Historical stats had no bearing on this week's edition of B/R's NHL Power Rankings, for which participating hockey staff assigned 32 points for a first-place vote all the way to one point for a No. 32 ranking, yielding the final 32-to-1 order that's presented here based on those compiled point totals.

Take a look at what we came up with and drop a thought in the app comments.

ANA | BOS | BUF | CAR | CBJ | CGY | CHI | COL | DAL | DET | EDM | FLA | LAK | MIN | MTL | NJD | NSH | NYI | NYR | OTT | PHI | PIT | SEA | SJS | STL | TBL | TOR | UTA | VAN | VGK | WPG | WSH

A prosperous 3-1-0 stretch devolved into a familiar script for the Canucks, who were down four goals against visiting Chicago before registering their first shot on goal. Goalie Nikita Tolopilo was pulled after allowing the four goals on 12 shots.

The losses are coming in all forms for the Penguins, who have dropped four in a row, including two by one goal apiece and two more by three goals each. "I thought we competed hard," captain Sidney Crosby said . "(But) it's a game of mistakes."

As if things weren't bad enough for the Blackhawks, they'll be without Connor Bedard for four months after the 2023 No. 1 overall pick injured his right shoulder while taking a faceoff against the Toronto Maple Leafs. He has 18 points in 15 games this season.

The Blue Jackets won the middle two games of a four-game road trip and ended with a solid effort, albeit a losing one, at New Jersey. "I really liked the last three games of (our four-game road trip)," defenseman Zach Werenski said.

It was an overdue return to the ledger's winning side for the Maple Leafs, who'd dropped nine in a row (0-8-1) before winning against the New York Islanders on Monday. "It has not been a fun time for anybody," coach Jim Hiller said .

Veteran Drew Doughty reached a milestone amid a mild turnaround for the Kings, who defeated Montreal in Doughty's 1,300th NHL game and picked up their third win in four games. "That felt amazing," he said . "The boys feel really good."

A brief resurgence has been followed by a return to recent normalcy for the Flames, whose Monday loss at Ottawa was their third straight (0-2-1) and dropped them to 1-3-1 in their last five. "We were the better team," forward Joel Farabee said, "but sometimes it's just really tough."

Detroit's Dylan Larkin Era finally ended when the disgruntled ex-captain was dealt to Montreal with two draft picks for three players and four picks. He had six points with the Red Wings in 10 games before a team-issued suspension in late October.

The optimism is back, at least a little, for Sharks coach Ryan Warsofsky, whose team had won three of four before a loss to streaking Minnesota. "We did some good things," he said . "There were some positives, but at the end of the day, it's a loss."

Cutter Gauthier continued to score, but the Ducks continued to lose. Anaheim's 3-2 loss at Seattle was its fourth in a row, but Gauthier moved within two goals of the NHL record for a single month (20). The Ducks are 6-6-0 so far in November.

An ugly beginning is just a memory for the Flyers, who've won three in a row and are 9-3-3 in their last 15 games since their atrocious 0-6-3 start. "This whole month we've been getting better and better," forward Denver Barkey said .

The nosedive continues for the Capitals, whose loss at Boston was their fifth in a row and also the fifth straight in which they allowed at least five goals. "We've got a great group in here," forward Tom Wilson said . "There's no panic in the room."

The Sunshine State was a mixed bag for the Sabres, who lost at Florida before winning at Tampa Bay a day later to wrap a six-game road trip at 2-3-1. "Offensively, we're starting to click," coach Lindy Ruff said . "It makes for winning hockey."

Returning to North America has been good for the Kraken, whose Monday defeat of Anaheim was their second in three games since being swept in two Global Series games in Finland. Joey Daccord made 24 saves in his first win since Nov. 4.

A two-game interlude was pleasant for the Mammoth, but another loss in Winnipeg made them 2-4-3 in their last nine games. "It's a reminder," winger Lawson Crouse said , "that you need to be ready to go right from the start."

The Jets were offensive in a defeat of Utah, getting a hat trick from Gabriel Vilardi to extend a recent run to points in nine of 10 games (8-1-1). "You can kind of feel like that was coming for Gabe," center Morgan Barron said .

The Islanders earned points in seven straight games (4-0-3) and outshot Toronto, 15-6, in the first period Monday before skidding to a 4-2 loss. "I'm not sure I've seen a game that (was such) polar opposites before," coach Peter DeBoer said .

Down three in the third period? No problem for the Blues, who beat Edmonton in a shootout for their fourth straight win in a stretch where they've scored 26 regulation goals. Prior to the streak, St. Louis was 26th in the league in goals per game.

The defending champs provided a reality check for the Rangers, who'd won three in a row and six of seven before a 5-2 home loss to the Hurricanes. "It's just an indication of where we aspire to go," coach Mike Sullivan said .

The Panthers got their sixth hat trick of the season from Sam Bennett in a win over Buffalo. That equaled a franchise record for a season and made Florida the fifth team in modern history to reach six hat tricks before its 25th game.

Nashville's run toward the top was stalled by losses at San Jose and Minnesota, but the rebound began with a defeat of Pittsburgh in which Juuse Saros made 21 saves. "For us, it was a must-win game," forward Jonathan Marchessault said .

The Canadiens and their fans had a memorable welcome for the newly acquired Dylan Larkin, who got an assist in a 2-1 loss to Los Angeles. "It was incredible," he said . "I'm so grateful for that welcome and to feel it on the ice."

What started as a month on the shelf for Nathan MacKinnon will now be 12 weeks after a new round of feedback from doctors extended the injury timeline. The team went 2-1-0 in its first three games without him, scoring nine goals.

He's the team captain and a fan favorite, but Mark Stone added a bullet point to the resume against Dallas when he became the franchise's all-time points leader. "He's the epitome of being a Golden Knight," coach Ryan Craig said .

Three losses in which they scored just four goals are only a memory now for the bounce-back Bruins, who netted 11 in consecutive defeats of Detroit (4-1) and Washington (7-5). Elias Lindholm had his first four-goal game against the Capitals.

Connor Hellebuyck's storybook start took some hits when he lost to Montreal and was pulled from a loss at St. Louis, but he bounced back with 21 saves on Monday against Columbus and became the fastest U.S.-born goalie to 200 home wins.

It's a familiar story for the surging Stars, who've gotten stellar goaltending during a five-game win streak, including a 33-save shutout for Jake Oettinger against Pittsburgh. "I'm pretty proud of this one," Oettinger said . "I'm going to enjoy it."

Frustration seeped in for the Lightning during a 6-2 loss to visiting Buffalo, when star forward Nikita Kucherov was briefly benched in the third period. "We wanted it easy," coach Jon Cooper said . "Tried to skill our way through a game."

It's been a while since there's been this kind of run for the Senators, who defeated Calgary to stretch a point streak to nine games (7-0-2), their longest since 2014-15. Goalie Linus Ullmark has won seven in a row at home and is 12-1-0 overall.

A trip that began with three wins ended with three losses (0-2-1) for the previously streaking Oilers, whose defeats at Tampa Bay and Carolina were their first regulation losses in road games this season. They're 10-2-2 away from Edmonton.

No one's been hotter over the last few weeks than the Wild, who ran a point streak to 15 games in a Monday win in San Jose and got a four-point night from forward Kirill Kaprizov, who's amassed eight goals and 24 assists in that same stretch.

Two games in two days? No problem for the champs, who scored seven times on 36 shots against visiting Edmonton before traveling to New York to whip the Rangers. Their 10th road win came in just their 13th road game, a franchise record.

articles.title: Trinity Rodman out of USWNT’s World Cup qualifier due to shoulder injury
articles.summary: Star forward Trinity Rodman sustained a minor shoulder injury during Washington Spirit’s 2-1 loss to Kansas City.
articles.body:
Trinity Rodman has not been included in the United States women’s national team squad for a qualifying tournament for the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027 because of a minor shoulder injury.

Rodman, 24, was injured on Saturday early in the Washington Spirit’s 2-1 loss to the Kansas City Current in the NWSL Championship Game — the Spirit’s third consecutive setback in the title match.

She was challenging for a ball when Current defender Laney Rouse collided with her midair and sent Rodman hard to the ground. Rodman left the playing field for several minutes and met with trainers before returning to the game.

Gotham FC midfielder Jaedyn Shaw has replaced Rodman on the 23-player roster for the CONCACAF W Championship tournament, which is a qualifier for the Women’s World Cup next summer in Brazil.

The USA squad opens the tournament on Friday against El Salvador in the quarterfinals in Mansfield, Texas. Eight teams are competing, with the four quarterfinal winners clinching the confederation’s four direct World Cup spots. Jamaica opens with Costa Rica, Canada plays Panama, and Mexico faces Haiti this weekend.

A victory for the Americans would send them to the semifinals on December 1, also at Texas Health Mansfield Stadium. The championship is slated for December 5 in Houston. The tournament also determines the region’s squads for the 2028 Olympics.

Rodman recorded 15 goals and 10 assists in a total of 33 games for the Spirit this season.

Shaw, who turned 22 on Friday, helped Gotham FC capture the NWSL Shield as the league’s regular-season champion. She scored 11 regular-season goals.

articles.title: CM Punk vs. Cody Rhodes at WrestleMania 43 Is Inevitable. Here's How WWE Should Get There
articles.summary: Cody Rhodes and CM Punk's blossoming friendship faced its first major hurdle on Monday's WWE Raw, when The American Nightmare revealed Seth Rollins as the fifth member of Team USA at Survivor Series.
articles.body:
Cody Rhodes and CM Punk's blossoming friendship faced its first major hurdle on Monday's WWE Raw, when The American Nightmare revealed Seth Rollins as the fifth member of Team USA at Survivor Series.

It was the unofficial start of a program that will ultimately lead to the two squaring off at WrestleMania 43 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

Here's how the two titans of the business should get to its grandest stage.

Punk entrusted his "best friend" Rhodes with his heart, and The American Nightmare shattered it by recruiting Seth Rollins for Team USA at Saturday's Survivor Series.

Rhodes turned to Punk's longtime adversary in the name of winning, choosing to bolster his win-loss record rather than preserve his relationship with The Best in the World.

This comes a few weeks after Rhodes told SmackDown general manager Nick Aldis that he wants back in the Undisputed WWE Championship picture after the upcoming premium live event.

Whether subconsciously or intentionally, Rhodes sacrificed friendship for his own title aspirations, so it is only right that Punk returns the favor.

Kevin Owens is currently chasing the undisputed WWE title held by Sami Zayn. In a year in which WWE Creative has played hot potato with the top prize on the blue brand, it should continue.

The Prizefighter defeats Zayn to win his first world title since 2016. From there, Punk and Rhodes are involved in a No. 1 Contender's match involving, for instance, Gunther and Finn Balor.

Punk picks up the win by pinning Rhodes with a handful of tights, the first escalation of tension in the relationship. When confronted backstage, The Second City Saint simply says, "It's all about winning, right?"

Dating back to the latest chapter in the Randy Orton rivalry, Rhodes has expressed a determination to get back into the WWE title picture. The personal feud with The Viper sidetracked him, as has the Team USA captaincy.

With Punk denying him a shot at the gold, he announces his entry into the men's Royal Rumble match at the beginning of February, looking to become the first three-time winner since "Stone Cold" Steve Austin.

Rhodes falls short, eliminated by eventual winner Oba Femi.

The American Nightmare has one last chance to punch his ticket to WrestleMania in another Triple H special: a multi-man match on a late-February episode of SmackDown (since Elimination Chamber has not yet been announced for 2027). A star-studded field competes for the right to challenge Punk, who defeated Owens for the Undisputed WWE Championship at the Royal Rumble.

Rhodes wins, beating Owens, Zayn, Gunther, Balor and Trick Williams, capitalizing on cheating from Zayn to score the tainted win.

Whereas fans rallied behind Rhodes as he sought to finish his story and win the title that eluded his father, they are less enthusiastic about his pursuit this time around.

Rhodes has had multiple opportunities and finally won a shot at the gold, only after someone else did all the heavy lifting. The fans boo him, not wanting to hear his passionate promos about winning the title back and for the first time, the jeers visibly shake The American Nightmare.

Punk spends his road to WrestleMania attempting to expose Rhodes for what he has become.

Whereas The Best in the World has been up front about how much the championship means to him and has not always taken the cleanest path to it, he tells Rhodes that he has become obsessed with the gold to the point that the "golden boy" of WWE feels almost entitled to it.

He reminds Rhodes that generations of Superstars have busted their asses to be the best. Bruno Sammartino, "Macho Man" Randy Savage, "Stone Cold" Steve Austin, The Rock, John Cena and Brock Lesnar never viewed the championship as something they were entitled to. They did everything they could, night after night, to earn the privilege of holding the gold.

From there, he drops the bomb that instigates the first pull-apart brawl between them, saying, "If you think I'm going to let some daddy's boy walk into WrestleMania and take this from me because he calls himself QB1, you're going to have another WrestleMania disappointment."

On the go-home episode of SmackDown before The Show of Shows, Rhodes takes a jab at Punk's time in All Elite Wrestling: "This is not the first time you've stuck your nose in something I built." He then guarantees he will leave 'Mania with the gold around his waist.

In the main event of WrestleMania Saturday, cameras catch Rhodes as he makes his way through the backstage area, preparing to make his grand entrance, when he encounters Randy Orton.

The Viper stands tall in front of The American Nightmare and, after some brief tension, looks him in the eyes and says, "You know what you need to do," referencing the punt that put him down at Crown Jewel in Riyadh.

During the match, Rhodes' desperation becomes evident.

An out-of-character low blow does not earn him the win, nor does a shot to the face with the WWE title.

A grueling contest between two of this generation's top stars sees Punk kick out of successive Cross Rhodes. Intent on winning his title back, Rhodes lines up and punts Punk. He wins the match and the title to a chorus of boos.

As The American Nightmare celebrates his win, Orton appears on the stage and gives him an approving nod, paying off a storyline that started six months earlier and resulted in the long-awaited Rhodes heel turn.

articles.title: World Ice Hockey Body to Challenge Russia Ruling by CAS at Switzerland's Supreme Court
articles.summary: GENEVA (AP) — Russia's legal win to return to international ice hockey will be challenged with an appeal at Switzerland's supreme court, the sport's governing body said Wednesday.
articles.body:
GENEVA (AP) — Russia's legal win to return to international ice hockey will be challenged with an appeal at Switzerland's supreme court, the sport's governing body said Wednesday.

The International Ice Hockey Federation raised questions about the impartiality of two of the three judges on a Court of Arbitration for Sport panel that ruled last month to end Russian teams' exile imposed since the full military invasion of Ukraine nearly five years ago.

The Swiss Federal Tribunal can overturn CAS rulings — and send cases back for a retrial — on limited procedural grounds, such as the integrity of judges .

The Moroccan soccer body is expected to take a similar legal path after a CAS ruling Tuesday to reinstate Senegal as the Africa Cup of Nations champion.

"Given the significance of the ruling and its implications for international ice hockey," the IIHF said Wednesday in a statement, it "considers it definitively essential to pursue the matter before the Swiss Federal Tribunal."

Swiss media reports suggested two judges hearing Russia's appeal had traveled to Moscow for legal conferences in the past 18 months. Those reports appeared after the CAS verdict and too late to contest the appointment of judges, who are selected by the parties to the appeal and the court itself.

One of the CAS judges, Guilio Palermo, also cited on his legal firm's website he was an investigator for the Russian-backed International Boxing Association led by Umar Kremlev, the oligarch now better known as a guest who helped bankroll the recent wedding of Donald Trump Jr.

The IIHF said its appeal to federal judges was "based on concerns around the independence and impartiality of two of the three arbitrators on the CAS Panel, especially following the information that has recently come to light regarding potential links between the two arbitrators and Russia."

Russian hockey's legal win at CAS has not guaranteed its teams can actually play in IIHF competitions.

Canada has refused to let a Russian team enter the country for the men's junior world championship next month. Several European ice hockey federations said they will boycott tournaments if Russia is allowed to play.

FIFA case set legal precedent at CAS for excluding Russian teams

The Russian hockey federation won its appeal at CAS despite the precedent of FIFA and UEFA winning a similar case at the sports court in 2022. FIFA lawyers cited inevitable chaos organizing a World Cup if Russia qualified and future opponents refused to play those games.

Challenging the integrity of a CAS judge before Swiss federal judges did work for Chinese swimming star Sun Yang who had been banned for eight years in 2019 at the sports court for violating doping rules.

Sun's case was sent back to CAS for a retrial with a different panel of judges, which also found him guilty and banned him for four years . He also challenged that ban at the Swiss federal court and lost.

articles.title: Desirée Vila, contra la violencia digital: "Un desconocido hablando de sexo y del cuerpo de una mujer no es humor"
articles.standfirst: En el Día Internacional de la Eliminación de la Violencia contra la Mujer, la atleta paralímpica denuncia el acoso a través de las pantallas y reclama compromiso social. Ella fue víctima
articles.summary: En el Día Internacional de la Eliminación de la Violencia contra la Mujer, la atleta paralímpica denuncia el acoso a través de las pantallas y reclama compromiso social. Ella fue víctima
articles.body: Hace dos años se hizo viral un vídeo que compartió la atleta paralímpica Desirée Vila en sus redes sociales. En él, hacía humor sobre su discapacidad, algo habitual en ella con el fin de normalizarla y acabar con los prejuicios. Lo que no esperaba era recibir numerosos comentarios de contenido sexual, alusiones a su cuerpo y mensajes que traspasaban cualquier límite del respeto. Hoy, 25 de Noviembre, en el Día Internacional de la Eliminación de la Violencia contra la Mujer, la medallista europea ha leído un manifiesto en Pontevedra en el que alza la voz contra la violencia digital, la que se esconde tras las pantallas. Es una violencia que no deja moratones porque no hay contacto físico, pero también duele, humilla e intimida. “Un desconocido hablando de sexo y del cuerpo de una mujer NO es humor. Porque estar en una red social no es una invitación a recibir acoso. Aquel día dejé de ser una espectadora de una realidad que hasta entonces conocía de lejos para vivirla en primera persona. Y fue también aquel día cuando comprendí algo aún más importante: yo no era una excepción. Porque mi historia no era la primera. Ni, por desgracia, sería la última", leyó. La deportista recordó los casos de otras mujeres conocidas que también han denunciado públicamente el acoso y los ataques recibidos en internet, como la atleta Ana Peleteiro, la cantante y presentadora Fátima Pego o Paula Vázquez. Pero quiso poner el foco, sobre todo, en aquellas cuyas historias nunca llegan a conocerse. Los datos reflejan la dimensión del problema. Según la Macroencuesta de violencia contra las mujeres, el 34,5% de las españolas de entre 18 y 24 años ha sufrido acoso digital en alguna ocasión. Una de cada tres. "Pensemos en nuestras amigas, en nuestras hermanas, en nuestras hijas, en nuestras compañeras. Y pensemos también en todas aquellas de las que nunca conoceremos la historia", invitó. Vila también quiso aprovechar su intervención para hacer una reflexión sobre los diferentes silencios que rodean a la violencia contra las mujeres. El de quien tiene miedo de contar lo que le sucede; el de quien recibe una amenaza y no sabe a quién acudir; y el de quien presencia una injusticia y decide mirar hacia otro lado. "Ese último silencio es el que no nos podemos permitir", subrayó. Combatir la violencia es una responsabilidad colectiva. "No reírle las gracias a quien humilla, apoyar a quien sufre acoso, educar en el respeto dentro y fuera de las pantallas y exigir a las plataformas digitales y a las instituciones que asuman también su responsabilidad en la prevención y en la protección de las víctimas", enumeró. La atleta recordó que la violencia digital no es menos real por producirse en un espacio virtual. "Detrás de cada pantalla hay una persona. Y detrás de cada persona hay una vida que merece ser protegida". Su discurso terminó con una llamada a la acción. Y no fue una expresión elegida al azar. Vila convirtió la palabra ACTÚA en cinco compromisos que deben asumir tanto la sociedad como cada uno de sus integrantes: acompañar a quien sufre; comprometerse y no mirar hacia otro lado; tejer redes que protejan y sostengan; unir voces y esfuerzos; y actuar ahora, sin aplazar la igualdad ni la lucha contra la violencia.

articles.title: Why The Lions And Cowboys Host NFL Thanksgiving Games Every Year
articles.summary: Here's why the Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys host NFL games every Thanksgiving Day.
articles.body: The Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys are always part of our Thanksgiving Day ritual. But why? Here's why the Lions and Cowboys each host games on Thanksgiving Day every year and background on their history playing on the holiday: Why Lions Host Thanksgiving Game The Portsmouth Spartans relocated in 1934 and became the Detroit Lions, but the franchise was struggling with attendance at the outset of the move, merely averaging roughly 15,000 fans per game. With that in mind, then-Lions owner George A. Richards got creative, spearheading the idea to host a game on Thanksgiving Day, which would be against the then-back-to-back NFL champion Chicago Bears. While the Lions lost their first Thanksgiving game to the Bears at the University of Detroit Stadium 19-16, the franchise had nearly twice the attendance of its previous games (roughly 26,000 people). The holiday game would become an NFL scheduling fixture, with Detroit hosting a game on the holiday every year since 1934, excluding 1939-44 due to World War II. The Lions are traditionally the first game of the day, with a 1 p.m. ET kickoff. Why Cowboys Host Thanksgiving Game The 1966 NFL season marked the Cowboys' seventh in the sport, with the team yet to make the playoffs or post a winning record. But that same season would ultimately mark the team's first playoff berth, as well as its first-ever Thanksgiving Day game. Dallas leaned in to having the holiday game and making it a yearly tradition because then-owner Tex Schramm saw it as an opportunity to showcase his franchise to a nationwide audience and ran with the publicity. Schramm also viewed the Cowboys hosting the game on a short week as an advantage, with standalone games outside of Sunday being a rarity at the time. Now, Dallas hasn't always played on Thanksgiving, as the Cowboys didn't play on the holiday in 1975 and 1977. That said, excluding the aforementioned two years, Dallas has hosted a game on Thanksgiving every year since 1966. The Cowboys won their first-ever Thanksgiving game in what was a 26-14 victory over the Cleveland Browns at Cotton Bowl Stadium. Dallas traditionally plays at 4:30 p.m. ET. How Lions, Cowboys Have Fared On Thanksgiving While it's tradition for the Lions to play on Thanksgiving, one might say it has become a cruel one for their fan base. The Lions are 38-46-2 all-time on Turkey Day. More notably, Detroit has lost eight of its last nine games on the holiday and previously lost nine consecutive games on Thanksgiving from 2004-12. Granted, the Lions had a four-game winning streak from 2013-16. The Green Bay Packers have been the Lions' most frequent opponent on the holiday, with the NFC North rivals meeting 23 teams on Thanksgiving Day; Detroit is 12-10-1 in these meetings. As for the Cowboys, they boast a 35-22-1 all-time record on Thanksgiving Day and have won each of their last four games on the holiday. Of those 58 games, a record 11 of them have come against the longtime division rival Washington Commanders, with the Cowboys 9-2 in those meetings. Now, neither the Cowboys nor the Lions invented Thanksgiving Day football, as NFL games had previously been played on the holiday. Rather, they're the only two NFL franchises that agreed to make the late-November Thursday game a permanent part of their schedule. There also wasn't a third game on the Thanksgiving Day slate – like there is now – until 2006. 2026 NFL Thanksgiving Slate This year's Thanksgiving slate is a doozy. First, the Lions host the Bears in a matchup between a pair of 8-2 teams in what's the NFC North rivals' first meeting this season (1 p.m. ET). Then, Dak Prescott and the Cowboys (5-6) play the NFC East-rival Philadelphia Eagles (3-7), as both teams try to stay alive in the race to win the division. This game will air on FOX at 4:30 p.m. ET. Rounding out the day, Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) have a showdown in Buffalo against Josh Allen and the Bills (9-1) at 8:20 p.m. ET.

articles.title: BYD conquista a Elsa Pataky con el Denza B8: "Puedo llevar a los niños, las cabras, los conejos, las gallinas..."
articles.standfirst: La actriz española es la nueva imagen de la marca china en Australia, donde reside
articles.summary: La actriz española es la nueva imagen de la marca china en Australia, donde reside
articles.body: No cabe duda de que BYD está de moda ya en todo el planeta. Su expansión fuera de China ha convertido a la marca en un protagonista mundial de la automoción capaz de atraer la atención... incluso en las antípodas. Allí, en Australia, se ha producido el último movimiento del fabricante asiático, que ha reclutado nada más y nada menos que a Elsa Pataky. La actriz española es la nueva 'amiga' de la marca Denza, el sello de lujo de BYD que recientemente acaba de iniciar sus operaciones en España (hace pocos días os presentamos su último coche, el Bao 5).. Se trata del cuarto modelo de la marca en nuestro país, después del Z9GT, su buque insignia, el monovolumen de lujo D9 y el deportivo Z. Pero en otros mercados hay incluso más gama. Entre ellos el denominado B8 en Australia que es por el que se ha decidido Pataky. Se trata en este caso de un 4x4 de lujo, con propulsión híbrida enchufable (recordemos que BYD fabrica únicamente modelos con enchufe, ya sean híbridos o eléctricos puros) y un tamaño considerable, 5,2 metros. Las prestaciones, pese a su tamaño y peso (más de 3.200 kilos, lo que hace que sea difícil que llegue a Europa), son más que respetables. Sus 578 caballos le permiten acelerar de 0 a 100 en nada menos que 4,8 segundos. Además, su tren de rodaje mixto le permite presumir de un alcance superior a los 1.000 kilómetros por depósito/batería (según el ciclo de homologación de aquel mercado).. Cualidades que encajan con las necesidades de la actriz española: "Es la primera vez que tengo la oportunidad de disponer de un coche sostenible de grandes dimensiones. Por mi estilo de vida aquí, en Byron, necesito transportar a mis caballos. El B9 es el primer híbrido en un coche grande que tiene potencia suficiente para tirar del remolque con mis caballos, así que lo estoy disfrutando mucho". "Es divertido de conducir, es un coche muy potente y tiene mucho espacio, como podéis ver. Puedo llevar a mis perros, las tablas de surf, a los niños, las cabras, los conejos, las gallinas, los perros, el pato... Sí, todo gira en torno a los animales". Además de potencia y funcionalidad, el Denza B8 también ofrece tecnología: "Mi función favorita del coche es el masaje", reconoce. "A mis hijos también les encanta. Cada vez que nos subimos al coche dicen: ¡Vamos a poner el masaje al máximo!", bromea.

articles.title: 4 Things To Know About Steelers QB Mason Rudolph With Aaron Rodgers Benched
articles.summary: Here are four things to know about new Pittsburgh Steelers starting quarterback Mason Rudolph.
articles.body: Christmas came early (insert cringe here). With the Pittsburgh Steelers announcing on Tuesday night that they've benched quarterback Aaron Rodgers, the team turns to Mason Rudolph, who will be under center for Pittsburgh's Friday afternoon home matchup against the Denver Broncos. Here are four things to know about the 31-year-old Rudolph: Rudolph Was A Big 12 Star Before joining the NFL in 2018, Rudolph was a star for the Oklahoma State Cowboys. Rudolph spent four seasons with the Cowboys (2014-17), serving as the team's starting quarterback over the last three years. Oklahoma State went 10-3 in each of those three seasons, with Rudolph averaging 4,255 passing yards, 28.7 passing touchdowns, 7.3 interceptions and a 160.0 passer rating per year, while completing 63.6% of his passes. In his 2017 senior season, Rudolph threw for a nation-high 4,904 yards and finished seventh in the 2017 Heisman Trophy voting. Moreover, Rudolph is first in Oklahoma State history with 13,618 passing yards and 92 passing touchdowns. This Is Rudolph's 2nd Steelers Stint Pittsburgh selected Rudolph with the No. 76 pick in the 2018 NFL Draft, with him serving as the team's primary backup quarterback from 2018-23, making a combined 13 starts, including eight in 2019. Over those 13 starts and 21 appearances altogether, Rudolph totaled 3,085 passing yards, 19 passing touchdowns, 11 interceptions and an 86.9 passer rating, while completing 63.5% of his passes. Pittsburgh went 8-4-1 across those 13 starts. Following a 2024 free-agent departure, Rudolph returned to Pittsburgh in 2025, with him since serving as the team's backup to Rodgers. Rudolph made one start last season. Rudolph Was In Historic Brawl As for the aforementioned 2019 campaign, which saw Rudolph make eight starts, there was one game (Nov. 14) that was among the wildest in the bitter history between the Steelers and Cleveland Browns — which is saying something. After being taken down for a sack by Browns superstar defensive end Myles Garrett in the fourth quarter of a prime-time game, Rudolph attempted to remove Garrett's helmet from his head. After the two players got to their feet and began to separate, Garrett instead got hold of Rudolph's helmet and hit him over the head with it. Chaos ensued with multiple fights breaking out. Garrett was suspended for the final six games of the 2019 NFL season; Steelers center Maurkice Pouncey was suspended two games; Browns defensive tackle Larry Ogunjobi was suspended one game; Rudolph was fined $50,000, with 29 other players being fined $3,507 for entering the "fighting area." What was said by Rudolph and Garrett during this fight remains a gray area. Rudolph Started For Titans The one season Rudolph didn't spend with the Steelers was when he played the 2024 campaign with the Tennessee Titans. In said season, which saw Will Levis open as the Titans' starting quarterback, Rudolph made five starts and nine appearances altogether. He finished the season with 1,530 passing yards, nine passing touchdowns, nine interceptions and an 80.1 passer rating, while completing 64.0% of his passes. As for the present, Rudolph has appeared in four games for the Steelers this season. articles.title: Patri Guijarro habla sobre su renovación con el Barcelona: “Los culés pueden estar tranquilos”
articles.standfirst: La jugadora del cuadro blaugrana afronta su primera convocatoria como capitana
articles.summary: La jugadora del cuadro blaugrana afronta su primera convocatoria como capitana
articles.body: Patri Guijarro es actualmente la mejor futbolista del mundo en su posición. Tanto en el Barça como en la selección saben que es una pieza fundamental para cosechar éxitos. En un momento clave en su carrera profesional, la medio centro ha atendido a Radio Marca en exclusiva donde ha mandado un mensaje de tranquilidad para toda la afición culé. Unas palabras necesarias para toda la gente que suspira por su renovación con el FC Barcelona. Pregunta. Muchos nos cabreamos al ver tu posición en la clasificación de los premios individuales. ¿Cómo lo llevas? Respuesta. Me halaga lo que dices porque valoras el trabajo que vengo haciendo y muchísimas gracias, pero bueno, a seguir trabajando. P. Una concentración diferente, con dos amistosos y el Mundial en el horizonte. R. Bueno, diferente quizás porque hay caras nuevas, muchas que vienen por primera vez, que se lo merecen porque están haciendo una temporada increíble, pero es que de cara al Mundial queda mucho y necesitamos también prepararlo realmente bien con todas las caras que puedan ir y que todo el mundo sea consciente de que en junio o julio hay un torneo muy importante, que puede estar ahí y que también conozca un poco cómo se trabaja aquí en la selección, porque quedan muchísimos meses. No sabemos qué puede pasar, que ojalá estemos todas disponibles y nos peleemos entre todas, entiéndeme la palabra pelear, pero también hay que tener otras opciones porque nunca se sabe. P. ¿Recuerdas tu primera convocatoria con la selección española? R. Sí, y además era sub-15, que yo no sé si sigue funcionando sub-15 o no, yo creo que no. Pero no había torneos, eran concentraciones, eran entrenos previos a sub-16, que eso sí que era habitual, que hubiese entrenos. Había como minitorneos, pero no eran Europeos y Mundiales como había en sub-17 o en sub-19, sub-20. Pero sí, me acuerdo perfectamente de que fue sub-15, luego ya fue todo sub-16. O sea, fue una vez. P. Después de todo lo vivido, ¿qué significa ser capitana del Barcelona y de la selección española? R. Por supuesto, yo siempre he dicho que venir a la selección, vestir esta camiseta, es lo que quiere toda jugadora y toda deportista. Y más después de lo vivido y, como bien dices, todos estos años, que lo dices rápido, pero desde sub-15 hasta ahora, más de diez años, y con el Barça igual, más de diez años llevo ahí. Y tantas cosas que he vivido que me alegro de... P. Se te ponen vidriosos los ojos. R. No, porque me alegro también de haber vivido el presente sin mirar a un futuro y ahora lo pienso, mirando al pasado, sobre todo lo pienso a nivel de que he aprendido muchísimo y he vivido muchas cosas bonitas y soy una afortunada. Y estar ahora en esta posición y seguir aquí, poder continuar con lo que llevo viviendo todos estos años, porque no es fácil seguir continuando a buen nivel, en el mejor equipo del mundo, en la mejor selección, pues es para estar contenta. P. En las categorías inferiores de la selección eras inseparable de Carmen Menayo. ¿Mantenéis esa relación? R. Sí, sí, sí. Yo con Menayo tengo muy buena relación. Es verdad que ahora, pues mira, por cuestión de distancia no nos vemos tanto, pero la quiero mucho. Muchas veces nos hemos visto en algún verano o cuando jugamos en contra, hemos jugado en contra. Nos tenemos un aprecio por todo lo que hemos vivido porque sí, como bien dices, éramos un tándem inseparable. P. Eres de las que imprime artículos de prensa y los cuelga en el vestuario. ¿Hay alguno después de los últimos resultados del Barça? R. No, de momento no he puesto. Sobre todo suelo hacerlo con cosas que sean motivadoras, que cuando hay algo que pique, suelo hacerlo así. Igualmente, también hay momentos que creo que sí hay que hacerlo y ya incluso desde dentro del vestuario a veces recibo un WhatsApp con el link o con una foto y ya me ponen a imprimirlo. P. Tiene que tener efecto, no puede ser siempre. R. Claro, si no te acostumbras. Igualmente, también hay que relativizar. Creo que en el club estamos viviendo un momento que igual siempre hay lesiones en el año, pero que estamos viviendo un momento que no es normal el tener tantas lesionadas. Y si ya partimos de que tenemos una plantilla algo corta, nos están ayudando muchísimas del B que están haciendo una temporada increíble y se están adaptando increíblemente bien, pero esa adaptación también se tiene que hacer y es normal. Entonces hay que relativizar. Aun así, no hay que olvidar que vamos primeras en Liga, que vamos primeras en Champions y creo que estamos teniendo muchos partidos buenos. P. Habéis marcado un nivel de exigencia tan alto que cualquier empate vuestro resulta extraño. R. Sí, es que nosotras somos muy exigentes desde dentro porque siempre queremos jugar bien, primero de todo, porque nos acerca a la victoria y queremos ganar. Es por lo que estamos las 24 horas siempre pensando en el fútbol y hacemos todo por el fútbol y por lo que cada día entrenamos y nos exigimos. Y, evidentemente, queremos mejorar cada día para hacerlo bien. Somos las primeras, pero también somos humanas. P. ¿Quién tiene un agapornis como mascota, Patri? R. Nadie, solo yo. Tengo dos agapornis. P. ¿Dos? ¿Quieren pareja siempre? R. Claro, y como viajo mucho, si no... P. Mira que podías esperar preguntas en esta entrevista, pero lo de los agapornis no. R. No, pero me gusta porque es diferente, es diferente, me gusta. Mira, todo vino porque, bueno, soy una amante de los animales y en la primera Champions, sí, en Göteborg, era muy pesada, pero muy pesada, sobre todo con Cata, con Pina, con Leila, que nos juntábamos mucho, con tener un perro. Les decía que quería tener un perro y me decían: «Pues adóptalo, tenlo». Y yo: «Ya, pero ¿qué hago?». O sea, viajamos muchísimo. A mí me da mucha pena que el perro esté cada dos por tres cambiando de casa. Bueno, pues ganamos la final en el 21, creo que fue. Mi cumple fue días antes y después de la final me regalaron un periquito. Y a raíz del periquito, que bueno, con los años se escapó, ahora pues tengo agapornis. P. ¿Se puede sacar a pasear a un agapornis? R. A ver, puedes, pero yo no lo hago. Yo los suelto por casa, son súper dóciles, muy cariñosos, muchísimo, muy intensos, no lo podéis imaginar. Pero hay gente que los ha paseado, ¿eh? A Mallorca me los he llevado, pero me los he llevado en un transporte, en el avión y todo esto. P. ¿Se mantienen las quedadas para jugar a juegos de mesa en el vestuario del Barça? R. Sí, por supuesto. P. ¿A cuál jugáis ahora? R. Mira, últimamente, el otro día estuvimos un rato jugando al Fortnite, pero fue nada, muy poquito. P. No vale que estéis promoviendo los juegos de cartas y ahora os pongáis a jugar al Fortnite. R. No, no. Mira, las veces que hemos quedado, normalmente el Brändi, que es como un juego de parchís, pero suizo. De hecho, la Eurocopa pasada nos lo regalaron las del equipo de Suiza. Jugamos en los viajes y luego alguna vez hemos quedado para jugar a lo mejor a algún juego suelto. No sé, es que no me acuerdo de cómo se llama. Pero tú sabes que está todo el abecedario y ya se elige un tema y hay que quitar las letras de todo el abecedario con el tema. O El Impostor, El Impostor mítico. P. Tus declaraciones sobre la renovación durante el acto de los cromos han generado preocupación en el barcelonismo. R. Sí, lo entiendo, lo entiendo. P. Después de perder a Alexia, existe cierta inquietud por tu futuro. R. Entiendo que estén preocupados, pero estamos al inicio de temporada. También creo que pude dar tranquilidad con lo que dije hace unas semanas, que las conversaciones están yendo bien. No todo va de un día para otro, pero sigo manteniendo el discurso, las conversaciones están yendo bien y pueden estar tranquilos. P. Por lo que me han contado, hay motivos para ser optimistas. R. Sí, pero ayer creo que era un acto donde eran importantes jugadoras y niños, Panini, cromos, historia... No lo de una jugadora individual. P. Entonces, ¿puede ser optimista el barcelonismo? R. Pues los culés pueden estar tranquilos. P. Si fuese la afición del Real Madrid, empezaría a hacer un crowdfunding para ficharte. R. Madre mía, si eso pasase, no sé, es que... No lo veo. P. Otra de tus grandes aficiones es el café. ¿Cómo te gusta prepararlo? R. Yo tengo una cafetera Sage. Yo voy cada día con brazo, café molido, de café de finca, y me hago el café con la Sage. A ver, La Marzocco es un pepino, siguiente nivel, pero quiero estar primero unos años con la Sage, aprender, que es una buena máquina. Pero sí, yo voy con café molido, café de especialidad y brazo, sí, sí. P. ¿Eres la mayor experta en café de la selección española? R. Misa, Misa. Esta es Misa, aquí me supera. P. Hace tiempo nos confesaste que te gustaría jugar algún día de portera. ¿Te has ofrecido ya? R. Ay, yo hace años ya se lo dije a Uri, al entrenador de porteras. P. ¿Has entrenado alguna vez de portera? R. He hecho alguna tontería con Cata, pero qué va. P. ¿Quién es mejor, Cata de mediocentro o tú de portera? R. Cata de mediocentro, sin duda. P. ¿Sí? R. Sí, sí, sí. ¿Pero no la has visto cómo regatea? Regatear en el área pequeña, ojo, ¿eh? Yo siempre le echo la bronca después. P. Ojalá que nuestra próxima entrevista sea en Brasil con una Copa del Mundo bajo el brazo. R. Ojalá.

articles.title: Super League: London Broncos confirmed as 15th team for 2027 season after clubs voted in favour of motion
articles.summary: Super League clubs voted to expand competition to 15 teams for the 2027 season; London Broncos now confirmed as club to take that place; the league previously voted in favour of two salary cap amendments that allow clubs more flexibility with young players and injuries
articles.body:
Earlier this month, Super League announced its 14 clubs had voted in favour of a motion to expand to 15 teams for the 2027 season.

Clubs were then invited to apply, with London Broncos - who had made no secret of their desire to be in the top flight - one of those to do so having completed the treble in 2026 during a brilliant season for them in the Championship.

"We are delighted to welcome London Broncos back to Super League for 2027," said chair of Super League Peter Hutton.

"This is an exciting moment for the club and its supporters, and an opportunity to build a lasting presence for our competition in the capital.

"They clearly impressed in the Championship last year, not only winning the League Leaders' Shield but the Grand Final and 1895 Cup in a memorable treble.

"In Grant Wechsel and Darren Lockyer, they have ambitious owners who are intent on making a success of our great sport in London and the surrounding areas.

"On behalf of all Super League clubs, I would like to put on record my thanks to both Grant and Darren for the collaboration they have shown over the last 10 days to enable the RFL to come to this recommendation.

"Expansion is about more than adding another club. We want a compelling, competitive Super League that reaches new audiences while continuing to serve the supporters who are at the heart of our sport.

"With more exciting announcements expected shortly around investment, broadcast deals and new commercial partners for Super League, we look forward to working with the Broncos as they prepare for 2027, and to seeing their supporters enjoy the elite competition in London once again."

After London went back down to the Championship in 2024, they were taken over by an ownership group including NRL and Brisbane Broncos legend Darren Lockyer.

Super League clubs approve salary cap amendments

Also this month, clubs voted in favour of two amendments to the league's salary cap regulations that allow clubs more flexibility with young players and injuries.

The first allows teams to claim salary cap dispensation if a player is injured for over eight cap-relevant matches, allowing clubs to sign a replacement player for the period.

It also forbids teams from claiming further salary cap dispensation should a player who was already exempt from salary cap implications becomes re-injured later in the season, unless he missed a further eight matches which affect the salary cap.

The second allows teams to feature a young player aged 23 and under - who has not previously played in any salary capped games - in two matches without triggering an increase in a club's salary cap spending, with that figure increasing to 50 per cent should they play between three and five matches.

Should the player feature in more than five matches, the full amount of their salary will be applied to the cap.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Trade Targets: Justin Boone's list of players to deal for before the default deadline
articles.summary: The Yahoo Fantasy Football default trade deadline is this week — it's time to make moves.
articles.body:
Creating realistic trade offers that lead to a deal being accepted is always challenging. Throughout the season, Justin Boone will be publishing his rest-of-season trade value charts, which you can use as a guide to help make moves and manage your roster.

Below, he highlights some of the players you should be buying before the fantasy trade deadline.

Daniels has been a solid fantasy producer this season, currently sitting as the QB8 in per-game scoring (19.4 fppg). However, aside from his massive Week 5 performance, which featured 103 rushing yards and two touchdowns on the ground, Daniels has only topped 20 points in two other contests.

Fortunately, he's trending up in recent weeks with a three-touchdown game against the Giants in Week 10, as well as 289 passing yards and 55 rushing yards versus the Bengals on Monday night. The only thing missing from his stat line in the win over Cincinnati was a trip to the end zone.

The touchdowns will definitely come over the next few weeks as he takes on the Cardinals and Titans, the two most generous opponents for fantasy quarterbacks. Daniels also has a date with a Falcons defense in the first week of the fantasy playoffs that's allowing the eighth-most points to QBs.

With rookie Antonio Williams emerging as a consistent threat and the Commanders flirting with adding Brandon Aiyuk, Daniels is poised for a strong finish to his 2026 campaign. Take advantage of his touchdown-less outing in primetime and acquire him before he goes off against the easiest fantasy QB schedule over the next month.

If you've been holding onto Jacobs this season, I have good news for you. And if you don't have Jacobs on your roster, it's time to trade for him immediately.

The Packers' lead back has been sidelined with a thumb injury that will likely cause him to miss this week's game against the Rams. Even if Jacobs were able to suit up in that contest, Chris Shula's defense has been one of the toughest matchups for running backs.

Thankfully, from Week 13 on, Green Bay has the fourth-best schedule for fantasy RBs, including the Dolphins in the first round of the fantasy playoffs.

Let's also remember, Jacobs finished as the RB10 and RB11, respectively, in his only two healthy games this season. While his rushing efficiency wasn't great in those appearances, his pass-catching and touchdown-scoring carried him to back-to-back RB1 results. As long as he's available down the stretch, Jacobs will be a major factor in fantasy title runs.

Burden is coming off his worst fantasy performance of the year with just two catches for 10 yards and another three yards on the ground. That's even led some managers to panic about his rest-of-season outlook, which we discussed on the Yahoo Fantasy Forecast earlier this week .

Needless to say, I'm not worried at all.

Prior to the down game against the Saints, Burden's previous four stat lines were 8-95-0, 4-130-1, 7-56-1 and 7-97-1. He finished as a top-10 fantasy WR three straight weeks, with the fourth outing landing him a WR16 result.

We're witnessing one of the best young wideouts in the league, playing in one of the top offenses the NFL has to offer. An instant bounce back is almost guaranteed against the Lions this week, in a game with the highest projected point total at 55.5.

Burden also has the seventh easiest fantasy playoff schedule, with potential shootouts against the Bills, Packers and Lions again. If last week's outing put any doubt in the mind of his current manager, it's your job to make them an offer they can't refuse.

It seems like a lifetime ago when Nabers posted four consecutive 100-yard games from Week 4 to Week 7. One of those stat lines occurred with J.J. McCarthy starting, which is notable since Nabers' production has declined in the three outings after the bye, with McCarthy under center.

Nabers has failed to top 55 yards in any contest over this recent three-game stretch, only saving his fantasy managers last week with a touchdown. However, the target volume is still there for Nabers. Over the first six weeks, he was averaging the seventh-most targets with 10.2. In McCarthy's four starts, he's fallen to 11th with nine per game.

A matchup with the rudderless Colts should be a nice remedy this week, followed by a couple tougher encounters with the 49ers and Seahawks. Then things get interesting with the Giants sporting the eighth-easiest fantasy playoff schedule, including battles against the Browns, Lions and Cowboys. Even though the last two games will be on the road in Detroit and Dallas, it's good news that they'll take place in domes during a time of the year when weather can be a problem.

We all know Nabers is an elite talent and even though McCarthy's presence lowers his ceiling projections, we're still going to see big days from the Giants' star wideout moving forward. Capitalize on this quieter stretch and make an offer before he gets back on track.

Jordan Addison, WR/T.J. Hockenson, TE, Vikings

The Vikings' passing attack is an entirely different animal now that Kirk Cousins is at the helm, but matchups with the Packers and 49ers have hidden just how much better the offense is with the veteran in town.

Justin Jefferson's improvement is obvious, but savvy fantasy managers can find other ways to make a buy-low investment before the value of players like Addison and Hockenson rise dramatically.

Minnesota has the eighth-easiest remaining slate for receivers and the third-easiest for tight ends. When we get to the fantasy playoffs, no tight end has a softer three-game span than Hockenson, highlighted by matchups with the Lions and Commanders in the first two weeks. Detroit and Washington are first and second in terms of most points allowed to tight ends.

With Addison sidelined due to a thumb injury, he's well off most people's fantasy radars at the moment. In fact, you just might be able to pick him up off the waiver wire, since he's still available in 41% of Yahoo leagues. However, once he returns, there is a massive opportunity waiting for him — evidenced by Tai Felton's 12 targets last week.

articles.standfirst: Emotiva y emocionante Gala de la séptima edición de los Premios Supera Iberdrola
articles.summary: Emotiva y emocionante Gala de la séptima edición de los Premios Supera Iberdrola
articles.body: Ana Peleteiro, Teresa Perales, María Pérez, Adiaratou Iglesias, Loida Zabala, Elena Congost, Belén Toimil, Eva Moral, Janire González, Laura Martínez, Desirée Vila, María Laborda, Inés Bergua, Lucía Martín-Portugués, María Corberá, Mavi García, Teresa Portela, Marta Fernández, Paula Sevilla, Blanca Hervás, Eva Santidrián, Daniela Fra, Rocío Arroyo, Herminia Parra, Sara Gallego, Ana Prieto o Carmen Avilés son algunas de las deportistas que estuvieron presente en la Gala de la séptima edición de los Premios Supera Iberdrola que tuvo lugar en el campus corporativo de San Agustín del Guadalix y que un año más pone en valor proyectos e iniciativas que representen y fomenten el deporte femenino y que impulsen la igualdad a través la práctica deportiva. Los Premios Iberdrola Supera hacen realidad muchos de los sueños que tienen a ellas, niñas, mujeres y veteranas, como grandes protagonistas. Hasta la fecha se han postulado más de 6.100 proyectos que podrían haber sido premiados, ocho de ellos afortunados en esta edición con un aporte de 50.000 euros, lo que eleva a 400.000 euros el apoyo real. Teresa Perales y Pilar García de la Granja entregaron el 'Premio Supera Difusión' a la Asamblea Nacional de Estudiantes de la Actividad Física y del Deporte en España. "Queremos romper con el silencio del abandono y que cada vez más mujeres puedan acceder o retomar la práctica deportiva", aseguraron las premiadas. Lydia Valentín y Jesús Carballo entregaron el 'Premio Supera Competición' al Club Halterofilia Alzira. "Somos un club pionero, con dos mujeres olímpicas antes que Lydia, pero qué mejor embajadora que ella. Tenemos un pasado, un presente y ahora con esta inversión seguro que futuro", dijo su presidenta. Eva Moral y María Pérez entregaron el 'Premio Supera Base' al Club Deportivo y de Acción Social 'The Brotherhood' de Murcia. "Es nuestro hogar, nuestra familia y un club de skate que han formado a campeonas, pero que también han visto a niñas que lo han dejado al no tener instalaciones. Nuestra obra va más allá del deporte, pues acoge a niños y niñas vulnerables. Convertiremos esta oportunidad en algo grande que merezca la pena", apuntó uno de los formadores. Ana Peleteiro y Mario Ruiz-Tagle [CEO de Iberdrola España] entregaron el 'Premio Supera Veteranas' al Club Remo Puebla. "En el remo remamos de espalda, nunca vemos la meta. Es algo parecido a la vida. Sólo ves el camino, lo que recorriste, el esfuerzo que hay detrás, todas las cosas buenas y malas", destacaron en el discurso. Desirée Vila y Susanna Griso entregaron el 'Premio Supera Inclusión' al Club Deportivo Uninsu de Lanzarote. "Gracias por hacer esto posible", apuntaron con mucha emoción. Sandra Sánchez y Paloma del Río entregaron el 'Premio Supera Social' a PGR ONG de la Cañada Real de Madrid. "Es un orgullo poder recibir un impulso tan grande. El deporte me ha cambiado la vida y me ha brindado un propósito que no estaba lejos sino al lado de casa. Miles de niñas ven que sus derechos fundamentales se ven vulnerables y ponemos al deporte como herramienta para una integración total y demuestran que sus sueños no son demasiado grandes por el lugar en el que han nacido", destacó Patricia García. Teresa Portela y Manu Carreño entregaron el 'Premio Supera Impulso Rural' al Club Piragüismo Río Jerte de Plasencia. "El deporte no debe depender donde nace una persona, sino hasta donde puede llegar", señalaron. Ona Carbonell y José Sainz Armada [presidente de Iberdrola España] entregaron el 'Premio Supera Salud y Bienestar' a la Asociación Deportiva Amazona de Cartagena. "Han sido ocho años de mucha lucha para poder mantenernos y continuar con nuestro proyecto. Estos premios nos han aportado felicidad y emoción, pero ser ganadores es un plus más porque soñábamos con este momento y nos habéis demostrado que los sueños se hacen realidad", finiquitaron. "Es un reconocimiento que se pararon en un momento de su vida y volvieron. Por las que están y las que no", añadieron.

articles.title: London Broncos to return to Super League for 2027 season
articles.summary: London Broncos return to Super League for 2027 after being confirmed as the competition's 15th team.
articles.body:
London Broncos will return to Super League in 2027 after being confirmed as the competition's 15th team.

The club will return to the top flight for the first time since 2024 after being selected following a decision to expand the competition from 14 to 15 teams.

The Broncos enjoyed a dominant 2026 campaign in the Championship, winning the League Leaders' Shield, Grand Final and 1895 Cup to complete a historic treble.

Super League clubs voted in favour of expansion earlier this month, with the Rugby Football League (RFL) then tasked with identifying the additional team.

London finished 16th in the 2026 IMG club gradings, below Championship rivals Barrow Raiders, who were initially considered for the available place.

However, Barrow and the RFL recognised the Cumbrian club would not be ready to compete in Super League in 2027, leaving London as the next candidate.

Super League chair Peter Hutton said: "We are delighted to welcome London Broncos back to Super League for 2027.

"This is an exciting moment for the club and its supporters, and an opportunity to build a lasting presence for our competition in the capital."

The fixtures for the new season will be announced on Thursday, 3 December at 08:00 GMT.

articles.title: Ronnie O'Sullivan: Seven-time world champion continues poor form with loss to 61-year-old Tony Drago
articles.summary: Ronnie O'Sullivan's poor form continues with a 5-3 loss to 61-year-old Tony Drago at the Snooker 900 Crucible Cup.
articles.body:
Ronnie O'Sullivan's poor form continued with a 5-3 loss to 61-year-old Tony Drago at the Snooker 900 Crucible Cup.

O'Sullivan lost to the Maltese former professional at the tournament in Reading, which is played in the Snooker 900 format that features a shot clock and frames that can last no longer than 15 minutes.

The 50-year-old had won his opening match, beating Barry Pinches 5-2 on Tuesday.

He was previously undefeated in the format, which is played outside of the World Snooker tour, having won the John Virgo Trophy and the Global Championship earlier in the year.

In a rare appearance in a UK ranking tournament last month, O'Sullivan lost in the first round of the Northern Ireland Open to Ka Wai Cheung, the world number 110.

The seven-time world champion subsequently lost 4-0 to Shaun Murphy in the Champion of Champions tournament in Leicester earlier this month.

He last won a ranking event at the World Grand Prix in January 2024 and, while he should reach the 2027 World Championships, he is in danger of slipping out of the automatic qualifying places for the 2028 edition.

World champion Wu Yize and reigning champion Neil Robertson were also both eliminated on Tuesday, losing to Joe Perry and Pankaj Advani by respective scores of 5-0 and 5-2.

Drago is a former world top 10 player who made his only ranking tournament final at the 1997 International Open, losing to Stephen Hendry.

He will face India's Advani in the final for a £25,000 prize.
